sources.design: International modified Delphi: 41 panel members, 28 final respondents; consensus on 41 of 58 statements.
sources.population: Athletes with bone stress injury; site, severity and sport demands affect management.
sources.coInterventions: Multidisciplinary bone-health/energy-availability assessment and structured rehabilitation.
sources.outcomes: High-risk consensus sites included superior femoral-neck cortex, anterior tibia, navicular and fifth-metatarsal base. Management/return varies by site, severity, pain-free function and loading tests.
sources.uncertainty: Expert consensus rather than trial evidence. Full recommendation tables not retrieved; no universal rehabilitation dose or permission to load an unassessed fracture follows.
sources.limitations: Expert consensus rather than trial evidence. Full recommendation tables not retrieved; no universal rehabilitation dose or permission to load an unassessed fracture follows. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: reported in accessible text: Indexed primary Discussion > Return to sports recommends structured physical therapy rather than one specified exercise; exact exercise mechanics/dose are not established.
protocol.supervision: reported in accessible text: Indexed primary Discussion > Return to sports places rehabilitation in structured physical therapy and multidisciplinary management. No fixed supervised-session schedule is reported.
protocol.progression: reported in accessible text: Indexed primary Discussion > Return to sports describes stepwise return guided by injury site/severity, sport demands and pain-free daily/sport activity, bone-loading tests and palpation. It does not provide a universal loading increment or calendar.

locations: Discussion > Management; Return to sports (indexed sections)

sources.title: Criteria and Guidelines for Returning to Running Following a Tibial Bone Stress Injury: A Scoping Review.
sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication; metadata firstPublicationDate 2024-08-14. Version/access details below.

access.details: Full Europe PMC XML retrieved and key methods, results and protocol tables inspected. Earlier PMC access was challenged where recorded in lower-leg-source-report.md. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC11393297/fullTextXML

sources.design: Scoping review of 50 sources, predominantly commentaries/reviews; recommendations largely level IV evidence.
sources.population: Return to running after tibial BSI; low-risk posteromedial injury differs from high-risk anterior cortex.
sources.comparator: Heterogeneous return criteria; no single controlled comparison.
sources.outcomes: Consider pain-free walking, tenderness, strength/loading capacity and radiological healing for high-risk injury. Tenderness criteria conflict; the 10% progression rule is not universally supported.
sources.uncertainty: Most sources are low-level evidence; tenderness criteria conflict. Later-stage resistance/plyometric suggestions often rely on other populations and do not establish acute-fracture safety.
sources.harms: No validated impact dose or harms rate.
sources.limitations: Most sources are low-level evidence; tenderness criteria conflict. Later-stage resistance/plyometric suggestions often rely on other populations and do not establish acute-fracture safety. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Individual walk/run after clinical criteria; increase distance before speed/intensity. Selected strength/plyometric work belongs to later rehabilitation.
protocol.dose: not established as one validated impact or resistance dose.
protocol.frequency: not established as one validated weekly frequency.
protocol.progression: Individual criteria and symptom response; universal 10% increment unsupported.
protocol.stoppingRules: Clinical healing/function criteria; do not transfer tendon or MTSS pain thresholds.

locations: Discussion > Return-to-Run Criteria; Evidence of Radiological Healing

sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication; metadata firstPublicationDate 2013-07-03. Version/access details below.

access.details: Primary manuscript available in PMC; indexed full Results, MRI grading/return-to-sport figures and Table 7 inspected. No randomised exercise protocol is claimed.

sources.design: Five-year prospective prognostic cohort: 211 athletes; 34 had 61 injuries, with 43 MRI-graded return records.
sources.population: Collegiate track/cross-country athletes under clinical care.
sources.comparator: Associations between MRI grade, BMD, anatomical site and recovery.
sources.outcomes: Grades 3–4 returned in 23.6 ± 2.4 weeks versus 13.1 ± 2.0 for grades 1–2. Higher MRI grade and lower BMD predicted longer recovery.
sources.followUp: Five-year cohort; individual injuries followed through return to sport.
sources.uncertainty: Prognostic associations and group averages under clinical care are not individual clearance dates or exercise-dose trials.
sources.limitations: Prognostic associations and group averages under clinical care are not individual clearance dates or exercise-dose trials. Research candidate only; no clinical release.
